Messages.Body:
An Independent, titled vampire going Anarch, most likely through
Secession, keeps their title.

http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/browse_thread/thread/b0bb7060c30c0f62/7f587bc039515aa3?lnk=gst&q=anarch+title+secession#7f587bc039515aa3

Aziz becomes Anarch through AS, then uses FS:Wherever to become the
Baron of Wherever.
Which of these is correct then?
1) His innate title gives him 2 votes.
OR
2) The fact that he has 2 votes gives him a title.

If it's 2, never mind.

If it's 1, does becoming a Baron then give him 4 votes?

No. You can't have two titles at once.

If Aziz had +X votes for burning X vampires, he would keep those
votes, because those additional votes are not a title, and so would
not be overwritten by the Baron title.

Messages.Author: Blooded Sand
Messages.Body:


Some Independent vampires may start with votes, as listed on card
text. Treat these vampires as if they had titles of their own.

Ok. So they have votes.
And they are treated *as if* they have titles, important for
Reinforcements et al.

But if you compare this to the rule for city titles where it states
that a prince/archbishop title is worth 2 votes, that means it is the
title that gives the votes.

The first example is treated as if titles, because they have 2 votes.
The second has 2 votes because they have a title.

Which comes back to Independent's keeping their votes during a title
change.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


The Independent vampire with two votes is treated as having a title worth 2
votes. The vampire is treated as a vampire with a title for all purposes (since
the rules specify no restriction), including losing that title if he or she
gains another.

> Which comes back to Independent's keeping their votes during a title
> change.

Which comes back to the answer that the votes from that title are lost during a
title change.
